title: {Syn} B-Trees Keep Databases Shallow
content:
B-trees store many keys per node, which keeps the tree shallow and reduces expensive disk or page reads. That is why they are a classic database index structure.

The branching factor is the trick: fewer levels usually means fewer random accesses, and storage systems care deeply about that.

Why it matters: algorithms keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
